verses.1: Having heard that, Rama, along with his brothers, felt great joy and then spoke amazing words to Lakshmana.
verses.2: O Lakshmana, these two sons of yours, Angada and Chandraketu, are skilled in righteousness and possess firm valor suitable for kingship.
verses.3: I shall enthrone these two in a kingdom, so let a suitable, charming, and unobstructed region be prepared where these two archers can happily reside.
verses.4: O gentle one, let a region be found where there is no oppression of kings or destruction of hermitages, so that we may not commit any fault.
verses.5: When Rama had thus spoken, Bharata replied, "This region called Karupatha is charming and peaceful."
verses.6: Let a city be established there for the great-souled Angada and another, very beautiful, moon-charming, and healthy city for Chandraketu.
verses.7: Rama accepted that statement spoken by Bharata, and having brought that region under control, he established a city for Angada.
verses.8: The beautiful city named Angadiya was established for Angada by Rama, whose deeds are effortless, and it was delightful and well-protected.
verses.9: And for Chandraketu, a city named Chandrakanta was established in the land of Malla, renowned as divine, just like a city of heaven.
verses.10: Then Rama, Lakshmana, and Bharata, who were unconquerable in battle, attained great joy and performed the anointment.
verses.11: Having consecrated the two princes, Rama sent Angada to the western region and Chandraketu to the northern direction.
verses.12: Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, followed Angada, and Bharata became Chandraketu's close supporter.
verses.13: Lakshmana, having resided for a year in Angada's territory until his unconquerable son was established, then returned to Ayodhya.
verses.14: Bharata also, having similarly resided for more than a year, returned to Ayodhya and worshipped Rama's feet.
verses.15: Both Lakshmana and Bharata, being extremely righteous and devoted to Rama's feet, did not even perceive the passage of time due to their profound affection.
verses.16: Thus, ten thousand years passed for them, who were constantly striving in righteousness and civic duties.
verses.17: Having spent their time with fulfilled desires, endowed with prosperity, and well-established in the city of dharma, the three brothers shone like three well-kindled fires of blazing splendor, properly offered in a great sacrifice. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे व्द्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 102 ।। Thus ends the hundred and second sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
